Role Overview

This is a hands-on, full-cycle role that owns the whole fraud control loop: investigate, analyze, set up rules, monitor, and improve. You will work tickets daily, turn what you find into data-backed fraud rules and strategies, monitor how they perform, and keep refining them. Each stage feeds the next.

You will own the card risk control strategy, from set-up through ongoing performance, and be accountable for the fraud rate and the interception rate.

Key Responsibilities

1. Investigation

•

Handle card risk tickets daily: review rule-triggered alerts, investigate suspicious accounts and transactions, and decide on block, decline, step-up, or card-lifecycle actions within SLA

•

Investigate fraud typologies: account takeover, card testing, BIN attacks, merchant collusion, friendly fraud, and first-party abuse

•

Assess merchant and transaction risk by MCC risk type, including high-risk merchants and non-card payment flows

•

Manage disputes and chargebacks end to end under Visa/Mastercard rules: evidence, representation, pre-arbitration, and arbitration

2. Data Analysis

•

Turn investigation findings into patterns: analyze ticket, alert, and transaction data to identify fraud trends, attack vectors, and coverage gaps

•

Measure false positives against loss to judge whether existing rules are effective

3. Rule Set-up

•

Design and set up fraud rules, velocity limits, and strategies based on the analysis

•

Make sure rule triggers and decisions stay compliant; escalate linked AML/sanctions concerns to Compliance

4. Rule Monitoring

•

Continuously monitor alert and ticket data after rules go live

•

Track and report KPIs: fraud loss rate (bps), chargeback ratio, approval rate, alert handling time, recovery rate

•

Keep the programme within scheme monitoring thresholds (e.g. VAMP, ECM/EFM) and support scheme and partner audits

5. Rule Improvement

•

Adjust, retire, and add rules in response to monitoring results, balancing fraud loss against false positives and approval rate

•

Feed fraud trends back to Product and Engineering to improve onboarding, 3DS, and authorisation controls

Requirements

•

3+ years in card fraud strategy or payments risk at an issuer, EMI, neobank, PSP, or card programme manager

•

Proven hands-on experience building and tuning fraud rules and strategies, not only working tickets

•

Hands-on knowledge of Visa and/or Mastercard dispute rules, reason codes, and chargeback timelines

•

Experience with MCC-based risk, high-risk merchants, and non-card payments

•

Strong data skills: SQL and Excel/Sheets to pull, slice, and explain fraud trends

•

Fluent English; Mandarin or other European languages are a plus

Nice to Have

•

Crypto-linked or prepaid/debit card programme experience, including crypto-to-fiat conversion at authorisation

•

Card risk control experience across multiple countries/regions

•

Experience launching a card programme in a new market or with a new BIN sponsor

•

Scheme monitoring programme remediation experience

•

Python or BI tooling (Looker, Tableau, Metabase)

•

Certifications: CFE, ACAMS, or equivalent

• Incident and prudential assessment: Support the prudential risk assessment within incident escalation: mapping incidents to notification limbs, preparing Decision Records on risk materiality, and drafting the risk sections of post-incident reviews. Standing member of the incident bridge.

Work with the best

We are Orderly, the ultimate destination for decentralized trading platforms. We are not satisfied with the limitations of centralized exchanges or the complexities of building decentralized order books. We aim to make trading easy, fast, and secure for everyone. How? By fusing the simplicity of CeFi with the power of DeFi.

At the heart of the issue lies “liquidity”. Builders often grapple with a paradox; traders need liquidity, but liquidity demands traders. Our solution is simple as is bold –concentrate all liquidity into one order book. One order book that connects all the liquidity in the crypto space.

Our ambition doesn't stop there. We're omnichain, championing chain abstraction. We envision seamless transactions, where the underlying blockchain is merely a detail. By concentrating liquidity, we aim to redefine the crypto landscape, making bridging and wrapped assets a thing of the past.

We are Orderly, and we are here to revolutionize DeFi, democratizing access to financial opportunities and fostering a fair, equitable paradigm for all.

About the Job

We are looking for a Salesforce Business Analyst to play a central role in our move from a legacy CRM to Salesforce. At IC, Salesforce is where our sales, retention, partner, compliance and support teams work every day, and the rules behind it are rich: who owns a client depends on their region, how they joined and whether they trade or introduce others, and what each team can see depends on role and regulated entity. You will be the bridge between those teams and our developers and QA, turning how the business really works into clear user stories, sound process and access designs, and an org people want to use. If you enjoy untangling complex processes, asking the question nobody has asked yet and seeing a requirement through to UAT, we’d like to hear from you.

What you’ll own

• Run workshops, interviews and process walkthroughs with Sales, Partners, Compliance and Support to understand how work is really done.

• Map current and future-state processes for the CRM migration, from sign-up through onboarding to trading, and identify gaps against the legacy system.

• Write clear user stories with acceptance criteria in Jira, plus BDD scenarios or specifications where a story needs more detail, traceable from business goal to delivered feature.

• Work with the Product Owner, Salesforce Architect, developers and QA to shape scalable solutions that follow Salesforce best practice.

• Contribute to defining data models, assignment rules and access requirements with the Salesforce technical team.

• Plan data migration with the technical team: field mapping, data quality rules and validation of migrated records.

• Maintain process documentation, data dictionaries, user guides and training materials, and drive user adoption after each release.

• Define and run test cases for system, integration and user acceptance testing, support production validation, and triage issues with QA and developers through to root cause.

• Use AI tools such as Claude to draft BRDs, stories and UAT scenarios and to surface edge cases, checking every output before it is used.

• Identify where automation or AI agents could remove manual work for sales and support teams.

• Define how success is measured, such as handling time, manual touches and conversion, and track it after release.

• Run demos and status updates, and communicate progress, risks and dependencies to management.

What you’ll need

Essential

• 5+ years as a Salesforce Business Analyst.

• Proven experience on a CRM migration or system transformation project.

• Strong knowledge of the Salesforce data model and core clouds, especially Sales and Service Cloud.

• Salesforce Administrator, Sales Cloud and Service Cloud Consultant certification.

• User stories, acceptance criteria and process flows that developers and testers can work from without guessing.

• A working understanding of Salesforce security: profiles, permission sets, roles and sharing.

• Experience in trading or financial services: client onboarding, partner management or compliance workflows.

• Agile/Scrum delivery with Jira.

• Effective prompting of AI tools such as Claude, including AI-assisted test case design for UAT.

Desirable

• A business analysis certification, such as Salesforce Certified Business Analyst, IIBA CBAP or CCBA, or PMI-PBA

• Data migration projects and large data sets, including Data Loader or similar tools

• Agentforce and AI-powered automation: defining agent use cases and taking them through UAT

• Brokerage or fintech experience: KYC/AML, trading account types, MT4, MT5 or cTrader, IB models

• Process modelling in tools such as Miro, Lucidchart or Visio

• Basic SQL or SOQL and Postman, to check data and API payloads yourself

• Multi-region, multi-language orgs

• Service Cloud experience, including CTI and call-centre integrations

• Brokerage or fintech experience: KYC/AML, MT4, MT5 or cTrader, IB models

OKX will be prioritising applicants who have a current right to work in Singapore, and do not require OKX's sponsorship of a visa.

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.

About The Opportunity

We are looking for a Product Manager with a deep understanding of TradingView users, strong commercial judgment, and experience driving product growth. You will grow OKX's business within the TradingView ecosystem by identifying the most promising customer segments, defining why traders should choose OKX, and finding effective ways to acquire, activate, and retain them, with accountability for measurable business outcomes.

Your first priority is to establish how the business can grow and which opportunities warrant investment. You will validate growth hypotheses through user research, data analysis, and focused experiments before committing substantial engineering resources. Those insights will shape the product roadmap, investment priorities, and the TradingView integrations and trading experience improvements you deliver with engineering and partners.

What You’ll Be Doing

• Define the Growth Strategy and Business Opportunity —

Identify high-potential customer segments, trading use cases, and market opportunities within the TradingView ecosystem. Assess competitive positioning, platform selection drivers, and OKX's differentiated value proposition. Build growth hypotheses and business cases that consider audience size, revenue potential, acquisition cost, and expected return, then set business goals, priorities, and a phased growth plan.

• Understand Users and the Trading Conversion Journey —

Use interviews, behavioral data, and community feedback to understand how traders discover platforms, use charts and indicators, set alerts, connect accounts, place orders, and manage positions. Identify what motivates or prevents users from choosing OKX, making their first trade, and returning. Develop customer segments and conversion funnels, and turn insights into clear product, positioning, and lifecycle opportunities.

• Validate Growth Hypotheses and Improve Conversion and Retention —

Design measurable experiments across acquisition, account connection, first successful trade, repeat trading, and reactivation. Use existing capabilities, onboarding, trader education, value proposition testing, and targeted campaigns to validate opportunities. Define success metrics, experiment costs, and criteria to scale or stop; expand approaches that work and use the evidence to inform subsequent product investment.

• Drive Go-To-Market and Ecosystem Partnerships —

Work with marketing, regional, lifecycle, and TradingView partner teams on acquisition and go-to-market plans. Evaluate ecosystem visibility, communities, creators, educational content, and joint campaigns as potential channels. Define the customer proposition, distribution approach, conversion journey, and partner objectives, and assess channels by the active traders, retention, and business contribution they generate.

• Translate Growth Evidence into Product Delivery and Integration —

Translate validated user needs and growth opportunities into a product roadmap, PRDs, and acceptance criteria. Define the minimum scope and engineering priorities required to achieve the business objective. Work with OKX engineering and TradingView technical teams to assess API integration, account authorization, market data, and order and position synchronization, and drive the necessary adaptation, testing, and launch to address specific conversion, trust, or retention problems.

• Own Business Outcomes and Continuously Refine Investment —

Own metrics for newly acquired trading users, first-trade conversion, active traders, retention, incremental trading volume, and revenue contribution, taking acquisition, incentive, and delivery costs into account. Separate the effects of market conditions, incentives, and product improvements. Review growth initiatives and feature investments, reallocate resources based on results, and track connection success and trading reliability as measures of experience quality.

What We Look For In You

•

Relevant product management experience in trading, fintech, or digital assets, with a track record of measurable product growth. You can explain how you identified opportunities, developed a growth strategy, and improved acquisition, trading conversion, retention, or revenue, including your personal contribution and results.

•

A deep understanding of TradingView users and their practical use of charts, indicators, watchlists, alerts, and trading workflows. You can explain why different traders choose a platform, switch terminals, abandon an order, or continue using a service, and validate those insights through research and data.

•

Strong commercial judgment and growth strategy skills. You can segment customers, assess opportunities, define differentiated positioning, select distribution channels, and build business cases. You validate demand and a credible path to growth through research and focused experiments before substantial engineering investment.

•

Strong analytical and experimentation skills. You can analyze funnels, cohorts, and retention, design and evaluate growth experiments, and assess incrementality, acquisition cost, customer value, and incentive cost. You can distinguish short-term trading volume changes from sustainable growth.

•

An understanding of trading products and their commercial drivers. You are familiar with spot and derivatives fundamentals and how instrument coverage, fees, liquidity, execution quality, and account and position workflows influence customer choice, conversion, and retention. You can translate these factors into product decisions.

•

Experience delivering products that involve technical integration. You have worked with engineers on API or third-party platform integrations and can read interface documentation, understand account authorization and market data, order, and position synchronization, define business rules and acceptance criteria, and drive testing and launch. You connect technical constraints and implementation scope to user value and growth objectives.

•

Strong English communication and cross-functional execution skills. You can work with TradingView partners, marketing, regional, product, and engineering teams on business opportunities, product priorities, and technical feasibility, aligning resources around shared outcomes.

Nice-To-Haves

•

Experience growing a business within TradingView or a comparable trading-tool ecosystem, with examples spanning opportunity discovery, growth validation, and scaling.

•

Experience with trader communities, creators, educational content, partnerships, or channel growth, with the ability to evaluate initiatives by active traders, retention, and revenue contribution.

•

Experience growing products across regions or trader segments, with an understanding of differences in user behavior, customer propositions, and acquisition approaches.

•

Experience with TradingView Broker Integration, Advanced Charts, Trading Platform, or comparable integrations, with an ability to explain how the work improved the user experience or supported growth objectives.

What Success Looks Like

•

An evidence-based growth plan that identifies priority customer segments, OKX's differentiated value, promising distribution channels, and the business opportunity.

•

Validated, repeatable approaches to acquisition, trading conversion, and retention, supported by research and focused experiments that guide engineering investment and resource allocation.

•

Measurable, sustainable growth in active traders, retention, and revenue contribution, with acquisition and incentive costs taken into account.

•

Delivery of the product capabilities and TradingView integrations needed to capture validated opportunities, with improvements to critical user journeys and ongoing measurement of their growth impact.

Perks & Benefits

•

Competitive total compensation package

• L&D programs and education subsidy for employees' growth and development

•

Various team building programs and company events

• Wellness and meal allowances

• Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

• More that we love to tell you along the process!

Role Overview
We are looking for a Senior Product Manager, Trading to own trading products on the Crypto.com App end-to-end. Retail trading is where users feel the product every day - and where volume, engagement, and retention compound. Every improvement you ship shows up in how people trade, how often they come back, and how Crypto.com wins share in a crowded market.
Your mandate is to drive trading products from discovery through launch and iteration: roadmap clarity, feature definition, customer insight, and shipping at global scale. 
You will run your roadmap with independence within Trading's strategic priorities. You prioritize initiatives, cut tradeoffs, and make the call on what ships when. You report to the Senior Director of Product Management, who sets strategic direction. You own the how and the when.
If you've shipped trading or financial products at scale, this will feel familiar. The difference is you'll be doing it at the frontier of crypto retail trading- perpetuals, spot, and adjacent markets- where the rails keep moving and the playbook is yours to write. No layers. No politics.
 


What You'll Actually Do:
• Own the Trading roadmap. You set milestones, surface dependencies, and keep strategic priorities honest. You make the prioritization call when everything can't ship at once.

• Define and ship trading experiences. You write the specs, run user studies, iterate on feedback, partner with QA on test plans, and clear the backlog. Nothing in your charter goes live without your sign-off.

• Stay close to how traders actually behave. You interview and observe customers. You ask "Show me how you currently trade and manage risk," not "Would you use this feature?" You distinguish what they say from what their behavior reveals.

Our Customer Experience function supports clients around the world across digital, written and voice channels, with teams operating across EMEA and APAC, including London, Krakow and Bangalore. Enablement is the engine behind our customer experience frontline. It makes sure we have the right people in the right place at the right time, that they have the knowledge and skills to resolve client needs first time, and that every interaction is fair, compliant and meets the standard our clients and regulators expect. The enablement team brings together three specialist areas - Workforce Management, Training & Knowledge, and Quality Assurance - and works closely with our regional CX teams, Compliance, Product, Data and our AI and Transformation colleagues.

Day to day, you will drive efficiency across the CX operation - making sure capacity matches demand, agents are ready and supported, and quality is consistently high. Looking further ahead, you will identify and deliver the longer-term opportunities for optimisation, from AI-enabled learning and automated quality assurance to smarter planning for a growing, increasingly digital client base. This is meaningful transformation work, not steady-state management.

• Lead and develop the Enablement function. Line manage the Head of Workforce Management, the Training and Knowledge Manager and the Quality Assurance Lead, set clear priorities and performance standards, and build a team culture grounded in accuracy, accountability and continuous improvement.

A junior Controls Analyst sits in the second line and does the groundwork that keeps the control environment visible — maintaining the inventory, gathering evidence, testing controls.

Risk and control framework

•

Maintain the approved control inventory, including control descriptions, owners, frequency and evidence requirements; process additions through the agreed governance process.

•

Map controls to processes, risks and applicable obligations. Identify control gaps, duplicate controls, outdated records and missing ownership for review.

•

Support Risk and Control Self-Assessment (RCSA) cycles by collecting inputs, checking completeness and recording changes to risks, controls and action plans.

Evidence and control testing

•

Request and organise evidence from control owners across departments, maintain an accessible audit trail and follow up on overdue submissions.

GRC records and audit support

Affiliate and KOL partners consistently promote the right products and bring in users who activate and transact.

The team can show results by market, BD, partner and channel, including first transactions, payment volume and revenue.

•

BDs know what they own and can execute with limited day-to-day escalation to Payments leadership.

•

Incentives support growth without rewarding low-quality acquisition or unsustainable partner spend.

•

Experience directly leading, hiring and developing a regional or distributed BD, affiliate or partnerships team.

•

A track record of building an affiliate or partner-led growth program from the ground up, including its incentives, processes and performance measures.

•

Strong knowledge of KOL, creator, affiliate and community acquisition, and the ability to judge partner quality and return on investment.

•

Experience managing a team against measurable acquisition, transaction-volume or revenue goals, including addressing underperformance.

•

The ability to turn business priorities into clear plans for a team and use performance data to change course when needed.

•

Commercial negotiation skills and the judgment to support important partnerships without losing focus on team performance.

As a Quality Assurance Engineer, you will join the Trading Data Flow team, responsible for integrating and processing trading-related data across Exness. You will be actively involved in the projects and initiatives of our cross-functional team.

We're looking for a Senior Staff Software Engineer to join our Payments Team, based in the Hong Kong. Payments is where OKX meets the real financial world. Our team has built and operates the infrastructure connecting OKX to dozens of payment channels across global markets, giving users deposit and withdrawal options that are fast, convenient, and — most importantly — trustworthy. That platform moves and safeguards user assets at institutional scale, continuously, across time zones and regulatory environments.

This is not a greenfield team looking for its footing. The team is established, the platform is in production at scale, and we are actively expanding — both in scope and in headcount. That combination is rare: you get the leverage of joining a growing team where your work visibly shifts the roadmap, along with the discipline that comes from a system already trusted with real money.

It's also an unusually good place to learn. Payments is a domain that's hard to pick up from the outside — every market has its own rails, its own settlement behavior, its own failure modes, its own compliance expectations. Here you'll work across a wide range of payment methods and channels, and you'll build the judgment that comes from operating financial systems where the stakes are real: how to design for correctness when money is on the line, how to reconcile, how to recover, how to keep a platform observable enough that you find problems before your users do.

You'll work closely with product managers, designers, and partner-facing teams, and you'll set the technical bar for the engineers around you — through design docs, code reviews, and the everyday habit of doing things properly when nobody's watching.

If you like the sound of a team where the problems are genuinely hard, the standard is high, and your opinion changes the outcome, we'd like to talk.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Design and build the core. Develop high-scale, 24/7 APIs and distributed payment services across multiple cloud providers, using Java and Spring Boot as the primary stack. Own systems end to end — from design doc through production ownership.

•

Expand our global reach. Help integrate and scale new payment channels and methods across markets, each with its own technical, operational, and reliability characteristics.

•

Protect user assets. Build for correctness first: consistency, idempotency, reconciliation, failure recovery, and the operational tooling that lets us stand behind every transaction.

•

Set the technical bar. Participate actively in design and code reviews, giving and receiving direct, constructive feedback. Help evolve the standards a growing team builds on.

•

Solve the hard problems. Investigate complex distributed-systems challenges and drive them to resolution rather than handing them off.

•

Partner across functions. Work with product, design, and partner teams across regions to turn ambiguous requirements into shipped systems, and to unblock dependencies before they become delays.

•

Grow the team's capability. Mentor engineers and share what you learn. Seniority here is measured in leverage, not just output.

•

Stay curious. Keep pace with a fast-moving industry and bring the good ideas back.

What you'll take away from this role

•

Deep, practical fluency across a wide range of global payment methods and channels — knowledge that is genuinely hard to acquire anywhere else

•

Experience designing and operating systems entrusted with substantial user assets, where correctness and recoverability are non-negotiable

•

A track record of shipping in a regulated, high-stakes domain at real scale

We’re hiring a Product Manager with deep UX and interaction design expertise to build social experiences around investing and trading at Kraken.


You should be comfortable designing flows yourself, building interactive prototypes, and working through interaction details with designers and engineers. You’ll also own the product decisions: which customer problem to solve, what to ship first, and how to measure whether the experience improved.




THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Design complete social journeys. Work through how someone discovers a person, decides to follow them, shares an idea or trade, receives a response, and returns. Connect these interactions into an experience users understand without explanation.

 - Make the interaction details work. Shape navigation, information hierarchy, copy, defaults, gestures, and feedback. Specify what happens when a feed is empty, a post fails, content loads slowly, or someone changes their mind.

 - Prototype before committing to a build. Turn ideas into interactive prototypes that communicate the intended behavior. Explore alternatives, test the uncertain parts, and give engineering clear flows, states, and acceptance criteria.

 - Use psychology to improve participation. Understand why people hesitate to post, seek recognition, follow strangers, or respond to others. Translate those motivations into decisions about audience visibility, prompts, reputation, feedback, and the effort required to contribute.

 - Observe users and fix what gets in their way. Run usability sessions, watch people complete tasks, and combine those observations with funnel data. Identify where people misunderstand the product, lose confidence, or abandon an action.

 - Design for first use and repeated use. Make the experience useful before someone has connections. Keep sharing lightweight during an active trading session, with clear control over what becomes public. Test the twentieth interaction as carefully as the first.

 - Connect design decisions to measurable outcomes. For each significant change, define the expected behavior and how to test it. Track task completion, abandonment, first follows, first contributions, responses, and subsequent retention. Work with data science to evaluate experiments and effects on both contributors and their audiences.

 - Take the experience through launch. Choose a focused initial scope, resolve trade-offs with engineering, review the implementation against the intended design, and use post-launch evidence to decide what to improve next.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - Has designed and shipped consumer social experiences. Your portfolio shows your contribution to feeds, profiles, sharing, messaging, discovery, or communities—and how the experience changed after launch.

 - Has strong interaction design craft. You can explain why a flow is structured a particular way, what users will notice first, what they need to understand, and which decisions or steps can be removed.

 - Can build realistic interactive prototypes. You use Figma, code, AI tools, or a combination to make behavior tangible and testable, including transitions, empty states, and failure states.

 - Understands behavior through evidence. You can show where user research challenged your assumptions and changed a design.

 - Can own product outcomes. You can prioritize a problem, define success, interpret funnel and cohort data, and explain whether an experiment produced a meaningful improvement.

 - Understands the context of social finance. You account for how credibility, incentives, reputation, and visibility of financial activity affect what people trust and choose to share.

- Lead and oversee day-to-day settlement operations across digital asset and fiat transactions.
- Ensure transactions are settled accurately, completely, and within the required timelines.
- Establish and continuously improve settlement procedures, controls, exception handling, and escalation mechanisms.
- Identify settlement breaks, operational risks, and process inefficiencies, and drive timely resolution.
- Support new products, transaction flows, and business models by assessing their settlement and operational requirements.

• Settlement System & System Architecture
- Develop a strong understanding of the end-to-end settlement system architecture and transaction data flow.

- Trading systems and order/transaction engines;
- Wallet, custody, and blockchain infrastructure;
- Fiat banking and payment systems;
- Data warehouse and reporting platforms; and
- Finance, accounting, and general ledger systems.

- Participate in system implementation, enhancement, UAT, and post-implementation validation from a settlement and finance-control perspective.

- Investigate and resolve reconciliation differences, including transaction timing differences, system exceptions, missing transactions, and data inconsistencies.
- Work with Product, Engineering, Data, Wallet, and Finance teams to identify root causes and implement sustainable remediation.
- Establish appropriate reconciliation controls and monitoring mechanisms to ensure completeness and accuracy of digital asset balances and movements.

- Own and oversee Fiat reconciliation across customer balances, banking/custodian records, payment channels, internal operational systems, and the general ledger.
- Ensure customer fiat assets and liabilities can be reconciled to relevant operational and accounting records.
- Investigate reconciliation breaks and coordinate with Finance, Fiat Operations, Product, Engineering, banks, custodians, and payment service providers for resolution.

- Balance sheet reconciliation;
- Customer asset and liability reconciliation; and
- Financial and external audit support.
- Identify gaps between operational systems and accounting requirements and work with relevant teams to develop scalable solutions.

- Establish key operational metrics and monitor settlement exceptions, reconciliation breaks, aging items, and resolution timelines.

In 2018, Bitvavo launched the first version of its digital assets trading platform, to bridge the gap between traditional currencies and digital assets. By offering transparent fees, a wide range of assets and an easy to use platform, Bitvavo is making the currency of the future accessible for everyone.

In eight years time, Bitvavo has established itself as the market leader in the Netherlands and one of the largest in Europe, with over two million users exchanging tens of billions of digital assets a year.


ABOUT THE ROLE

People trust Bitvavo with their money, their digital assets and their personal data. Your job is to make sure that trust is always deserved.

We are seeking a strong Data Protection Officer to drive and continuously develop Bitvavo's data protection program, ensuring compliance with data protection and privacy laws including the GDPR. Reporting to the Head of Legal, you will work closely with multiple business units and products to keep Bitvavo compliant across all areas of data protection, as part of the legal team based in Amsterdam. You will own the business processes and policies covering data access, classification, quality and life cycle management.

This is a senior, hands-on role for someone ready to lead the DPO function independently, comfortable making decisions and engaging directly with regulators and with stakeholders at every level, including our Management Board.


WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

This role requires a broad understanding of data protection law, including knowing when to bring in outside expertise. You will provide independent oversight of Bitvavo's compliance with data protection legislation, with real scope to shape our data strategy.

 - Advise and guide Bitvavo on the policies and standards needed to meet its data protection obligations

 - Engage with data protection authorities, including regular briefings, and maintain accurate records demonstrating GDPR compliance

 - Organise training and awareness activities on data protection and privacy across the company

 - Build a culture that embeds respect for data protection and privacy, acting as the champion for compliance

 - Communicate the privacy implications of new technology and proof of concepts clearly, to both technical and non-technical audiences

 - Assist in addressing mandatory notification and other legal issues in the event of a data loss or breach

 - Challenge the status quo with creative, pragmatic solutions to difficult data protection problems, including on innovative ecommerce and AI projects

 - Devise privacy preserving methods for using large structured, unstructured, transactional and real time data sets, and turn data protection law, statistics and business judgement into actionable recommendations


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

This role requires a qualified lawyer holding a law degree, with at least 7 years of experience in data protection including a minimum of 5 years gained within the EU, which is mandatory given the EU specific nature of this regulation. Experience within the Dutch market of 5 years or more is a strong preference.

 - Proven record of engaging directly with data protection authorities on compliance matters

 - Experience handling data protection and privacy issues for a regulated entity, ideally in tech or ecommerce

 - Strong knowledge of and interest in emerging technologies and their social and economic impact, including customer facing ecommerce

 - Proven ability to analyze complex legal, regulatory and business issues and give sound advice under time pressure

 - Experience managing multiple compliance projects, frameworks or teams, including internal and external resources and delivering training

 - Knowledge of IT security and data analysis methodologies, with experience working alongside IT Security teams in a data driven business

 - A strategic, open minded and user centered thinker, who communicates proactively, connects the dots across industry and regulatory trends, and stays focused on execution

At Bitvavo, we believe that diverse perspectives drive innovation, foster creativity, and lead to better outcomes. We are committed to building a team that reflects the diversity of the communities we serve and creating an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, identities, and experiences. Regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, age, religion, ability, or any other characteristic. Join us and be part of a team that values and celebrates your unique contributions.

Bitvavo does not accept resumes from staffing, search, or recruitment firms without a signed agreement. If you send us a resume without such an agreement, we may contact the candidate directly without any obligation whatsoever and no fee of any kind will be paid should we hire the candidate.


WHAT WE OFFER

At Bitvavo, we believe in attracting, motivating and retaining talented people through market-competitive offerings that go beyond compensation alone. To learn more about our total rewards package and the benefits we offer, visit our Life at Bitvavo page.

Set the vision, priorities, operating model, and quality standards for Product Analytics.

Hire, coach, and develop a high-performing team.

Review analytical and data-engineering PRs, providing guidance on SQL, data models, pipelines, metric definitions, and methodology.

Represent Product Analytics in executive and product decision-making.

Allocate team capacity toward the company’s highest-impact opportunities.

Partner with Product, Engineering, Data, CRM, Growth, and other functions to align definitions, priorities, and business interpretation.

Make experimentation and evidence core parts of product development.

Establish standards for hypotheses, success metrics, guardrails, experiment design, causal interpretation, and rollout decisions.

Use AI and automation to streamline experiment intake, validation, analysis, and readouts while maintaining analytical rigor.

Help product teams move from opinion-led decisions to repeatable test-and-learn practices.

Set standards for product instrumentation and ensure new releases can be measured reliably.

Job TitleSenior Manager, Prudential Risk

Job Description
So, who are we?
IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in
established businesses.

The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.

Join us at IG – the future gets built here

Your Team:
This is a technically demanding, high-visibility role at the core of IG's second line of defence. As Senior Manager, Prudential Risk, you will be IG's in-house expert on capital adequacy and prudential regulation — owning the ICARA process end-to-end and ensuring IG's regulatory submissions to the FCA meet the highest standards of rigour.
Working in close partnership with Finance and the wider Risk function, you will translate complex regulatory requirements into well-governed capital planning processes. This is a role for a rare combination: quantitative capability, regulatory fluency, and the credibility to engage confidently with the FCA, senior management, and Board-level committees.

What you'll do:
ICARA Process Execution
• Own and execute IG's Internal Capital Adequacy and Risk Assessment (ICARA) process end-to-end, coordinating risk assessments, wind-down analysis, and capital and liquidity adequacy assessments across the Group.
• Design and run stress testing programmes that credibly challenge IG's capital position under a range of macroeconomic, market, and idiosyncratic scenarios.
• Produce the ICARA document to a standard that withstands FCA scrutiny, incorporating clear narrative, robust quantitative analysis, and well-evidenced conclusions.
• Drive continuous improvement of the ICARA methodology, embedding lessons from regulatory feedback and evolving best practice.

Capital Modelling & Quantitative Methodology
• Develop and maintain IG's capital models, covering Pillar 1 own funds requirements, Pillar 2 add-ons, and operational risk capital quantification.
• Build and refine quantitative risk methodologies, including scenario analysis frameworks, tail loss modelling, and sensitivity analysis tools.
• Maintain model documentation to the standard required for internal governance and regulatory review, ensuring assumptions, limitations, and calibration are clearly articulated.
• Monitor MIFIDPRU developments and FCA thematic reviews, assessing implications for IG's capital models and ensuring methodologies remain current.

Regulatory Submissions & Engagement
• Prepare regulatory submissions and associated documentation for FCA requirements, including ICARA submissions, regulatory returns, and responses to supervisory requests.
• Act as subject matter expert during regulatory examinations and thematic reviews, presenting IG's capital assessment approach with clarity and authority.
• Draft IG's responses to FCA consultations relevant to prudential regulation, identifying practical implications and setting out well-reasoned positions.
• Maintain current knowledge of MIFIDPRU, CRD/CRR developments, and FCA supervisory priorities, translating requirements into actionable internal guidance.

Capital Planning & Finance Partnership
• Partner closely with Finance on capital planning, forecasting, and ongoing monitoring, ensuring risk and finance perspectives are well integrated in IG's capital management process.
• Produce regular capital adequacy MI for Risk Committee and Board, providing clear analysis of headroom, sensitivities, and emerging risks to the capital position.
• Support strategic initiatives and M&A activity by providing capital impact assessments and scenario modelling as required.
• Contribute to wind-down planning and recovery analysis, ensuring capital and liquidity adequacy under stress is well-evidenced and clearly documented.

Key Deliverables & Outcomes
• An ICARA process and document that is robust, well-governed, and consistently meets FCA expectations.
• Capital models and quantitative methodologies that are credible, well-documented, and subject to appropriate governance.
• Regulatory submissions of the highest quality, produced on time and to standard.
• A stress testing programme that provides genuine insight into IG's capital resilience across a range of scenarios.
• Strong, trusted relationships with Finance enabling integrated and forward-looking capital planning.
• Clear, actionable capital adequacy MI that supports informed decision-making at committee and Board level.

What you'll need:
Professional Experience
• Significant experience in prudential risk, capital management, or a related quantitative risk discipline within financial services, gained in a second-line, regulatory, or specialist advisory capacity.
• Deep, hands-on knowledge of MIFIDPRU and the ICARA process, including capital adequacy assessment, wind-down analysis, and stress testing.
• Proven track record of developing and maintaining capital models and quantitative risk methodologies, with strong model governance practices.
• Experience preparing regulatory submissions and engaging directly with the FCA or PRA on prudential matters.
• Demonstrated ability to partner with Finance on capital planning and forecasting processes.
• A relevant professional qualification (e.g. CFA, FRM, ACA, or equivalent) is advantageous but not essential.

Skills & Attributes
• Quantitatively strong — comfortable building and stress-testing models, interpreting outputs critically, and communicating uncertainty with appropriate nuance.
• Regulatory fluency — able to navigate complex rulebooks and translate technical requirements into clear, practical guidance for a business audience.
• Precise communicator — produces written work of the quality required for regulatory submission and Board-level consumption.
• Commercially aware — understands business drivers and calibrates capital assessments to reflect real-world constraints and strategic priorities.
• Collaborative and influential — builds trusted cross-functional relationships, particularly with Finance, and operates effectively without direct authority.
• Follows IG's five performance principles: Lead and Inspire, Think Big, Champion the Client, Deliver at Pace, and Raise the Bar.

Why IG Group:
Technical Depth & Regulatory Relevance: Own a genuinely complex prudential risk remit at a regulated FTSE 100 firm, with direct FCA engagement and high visibility across Risk and Finance leadership.
Strategic Consequence: Your capital analysis and ICARA outputs feed directly into Board-level decisions on capital deployment and regulatory standing — a role where analytical quality has real business impact.
Evolving Regulatory Landscape: Engage with a fast-moving prudential agenda including MIFIDPRU embedding, operational resilience capital requirements, and emerging FCA supervisory priorities.
Collaborative Environment: Work alongside a strong Risk and Finance community in a business that values rigour, pragmatism, and continuous improvement in equal measure.
Competitive Rewards: A competitive package including salary, performance-related bonus, and a comprehensive benefits suite within a dynamic, growth-oriented global business.

The Perks
It really is more than a job. We think like a start-up, but we deliver like a FTSE 100 — so the bar is high, and we won't pretend otherwise. We work hybrid, which means three days in the office. We’ll recognise your talent and make sure that you can still have a life – at work, and outside of it. Networks, committees, awards, sports and social clubs, mentorships, volunteering opportunities, extra time off… the list goes on.

• Flexible Benefits Package on top of your salary (12%)
• Private medical cover for you and your family
• Life insurance
• Contribution to gym memberships
• 25 Days holiday, with 1 additional day off to celebrate your Birthday & 2 additional days off a year for voluntary work (28 in total)
• The option to buy or sell holiday days

IG Group is a FTSE 100 fintech operating across five continents, serving over 1.4m customers and handling billions of dollars in transactions – built on scale, trust, and proof. We didn't pivot to innovation; it's how we've always operated. What that means for the people who work here is real: genuinely complex problems to solve, the technology and resources to tackle them properly, and the kind of scope that's rare in established businesses.

The bar is high – bring a curious and forward-thinking mindset and we'll give you the platform to define what comes next.

Join us at IG – the future gets built here.

Your Team
• Journey Transformation owns the end-to-end journeys that clients and colleagues move through: onboarding, funding, trading, servicing, disputes and account closure on the client side, and the operational workflows that sit behind all of them.

Your role in the Team’s Success
• Our job is to find where those journeys break, prove what the breakage costs, and drive the fix through to a measured result.
• Digital servicing and conversational AI are one lever we pull. Process redesign, channel change, automation, system configuration, policy change and eliminating steps at source are others. The lever follows the diagnosis, never the reverse.
• You are the engine of that mission. You work out where friction and servicing demand are really coming from, build the evidence for what will remove them, and drive those changes through to delivery and proven results. Working directly alongside the Head of Journey Transformation in a small core team, you will help establish our journey intelligence capability from the ground up: the mapping standards, the diagnostic methods and the evidence bar the team is held to.
• Change runs down two routes. Some is delivered directly within Operations, through our servicing and contact centre technology estate - and you will own that end to end. Some belongs on the roadmaps of other teams, such as app and web product, platform APIs, marketing or compliance, and has to earn its place there on the strength of the evidence behind it - so you will build cases strong enough to do that, then carry them through the governance that prioritises them.

This is not a documentation role. The mandate is change shipped and results proven.

What success looks like
